postTitle: Gig and Informal Work: Planning Without an Employer
topic: Uneven freelance income can become a steady monthly salary

assumptions.notes: One freelance year, monthly income: Jan €1,800, Feb €4,200, Mar €900, Apr €3,600, May €2,700, Jun €5,100, Jul €1,200, Aug €3,300, Sep €2,400, Oct €4,500, Nov €600, Dec €3,900. Total €34,200. 25% set aside for tax (illustrative): €8,550. Left after tax €25,650, about €2,140 a month (25,650 ÷ 12 = 2,137.5). Fixed salary €2,000 a month, €24,000 a year. Holding account running balance lowest at €825 below zero in March; year ends €1,650 ahead (25,650 minus 24,000). Illustrative.

hookVariants.narration: Your income swings from six hundred to five thousand one hundred euros. Your rent doesn't. What do you pay yourself?

beats.narration: One freelance year: thirty four thousand two hundred euros.
Every payment lands in the same account; a quarter is set aside for tax.
Then the same two thousand euros goes out each month, drawing on a starting buffer.
The salary method: one account, tax first, a fixed salary on a fixed date.

caption.instagram:
Your income swings from €600 to €5,100. Your rent doesn't. So what do you pay yourself?

One freelance year: €34,200, no two months alike. Every payment lands in one account, 25% is set aside for tax on arrival, and a fixed €2,000 goes out each month. Starting from a €2,000 buffer, the account never fell below about €1,175 and ended the year €1,650 higher.
